selector.rationale: Positive lupus anticoagulant, elevated anticardiolipin IgM, and anti-phosphatidylserine IgM support antiphospholipid syndrome, which best explains the thrombotic vasculopathy and other clinical findings

rejected.label: Infectious mononucleosis
rejected.why: Epstein-Barr virus DNA PCR positivity is not sufficient to explain the full clinical picture, particularly the thrombotic vasculopathy

rejected.label: Vasculitis
rejected.why: Lack of significant neutrophils or leukocytoclasia on skin biopsy and negative tests for antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies and anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies make vasculitis less likely

rejected.label: Respiratory syncytial virus infection
rejected.why: While the patient has a positive FilmArray respiratory panel for respiratory syncytial virus, this does not fully account for the systemic symptoms and thrombotic vasculopathy
